text:
• Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are widely used in real-world applications

• Examples include:
– Health monitoring (patient tracking systems)
– Battlefield surveillance (enemy movement detection)
– Environmental monitoring (air pollution, forest fire detection, tsunami alerts)

• In many scenarios, sensors are deployed in remote or dangerous locations
• Battery replacement is difficult or impossible

name: Content Placeholder 2
text:
Energy Limitation & Scheduling Concept

1.Each sensor operates on a limited battery
2. Continuous operation quickly drains energy
• To save energy:
– Sensors are divided into groups (covers)
– Each group can independently monitor the environment
• Groups are activated one at a time, others remain inactive
Real-Life Example:
Like CCTV cameras in a city working in shifts instead of all running together

name: TextBox 2
text:
Boosting an evolution strategy with a preprocessing step: application to group scheduling problem in directional sensor networks[1]
Methodology Proposed
The paper proposes a two-membered Evolution Strategy ((1+1)-ES) based approach (ES-TRMP) for solving TRMP.
Research Gap
Existing methods mainly use evolutionary or greedy techniques, but they do not incorporate learning-based adaptive decision making.
Current approaches also lack mechanisms to dynamically learn better scheduling strategies during the search process.

name: TextBox 6
text:
• The proposed RL-based approach performs well for small and medium instances
• However, for large-scale problems (high number of groups):
– Execution time increases significantly
– Computational overhead of RL becomes higher
– Cost improvements are not always consistent
• RL requires sufficient iterations to learn good policies, which increases runtime
